question.prompt:
There are \(81\) grid points (uniformly spaced) in the square shown in the diagram below, including the points on the edges. Point \(P\) is in the center of the square. Given that point \(Q\) is randomly chosen among the other \(80\) points, what is the probability that the line \(PQ\) is a line of symmetry for the square?

[Figure 1](figures/2019_AMC_8_Q06_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
A square has four lines of symmetry: the horizontal and vertical lines through its center, and its two diagonals. The line \(PQ\) works exactly when \(Q\) lies on one of these lines.

[Figure 1](figures/2019_AMC_8_Q06_official_expansion_solution_fig1.png)

There are \(9\) points across each row because the grid has \(9^2=81\) points. Each symmetry line contains \(9\) grid points, including \(P\), so it supplies \(8\) choices for \(Q\). The four lines meet only at \(P\), which is excluded; thus no eligible point is counted twice.

There are \(4\cdot8=32\) favorable choices among \(80\) equally likely choices. The probability is

\[
\frac{32}{80}=\boxed{\frac25},
\]

choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Count grid points on the four square symmetry axes without overlap
